title: Scene model: domain objects, tracks, and lowering to primitives

notes.author: Jack Roddy/89ec73b0
notes.text: A scene is a canvas (width, height in pixels, fps, duration in seconds, background) plus objects in paint order. Objects are domain objects, grid and plot first, not bare shapes. Every animatable property is a Track<T>: Constant(T) or Keyframes of (time, value, easing) with easings linear, ease-in, ease-out, ease-in-out and hold; discrete values such as cell text only step. Sampling an object at time t lowers it to primitives (rect, ellipse, line, polyline, path, text), and the renderer draws primitives only, so lowering is unit-testable without pixels. Grid: rows x cols, cell size, origin; per cell a value, fill, text color and an offset track for swaps. Plot: x and y range, ticks and labels; series of line, scatter or bars; a reveal fraction to draw a line over time. Each object has an optional lifetime [start, end). Out of the first version: groups and nested transforms, path morphing, expressions linking properties, audio.
